questions.topic: ML: the fraud label has no behavioral signal
questions.question: On the full 2023 to 2026 history the leak-free model and the rules baseline both score ROC AUC 0.50 on 1.5 million held-out rows: is_fraud is flat across every feature and only the leaked fraud_score separates it. How do we present the learned component? (a) Report the negative result with the pipeline as evidence; (b) train the same pipeline on a proxy target with real structure, if we find one; (c) keep the rules baseline as the risk signal and say why.
questions.context: docs/technical-discuss-points.md section 5 and reports/ml_full/fraud_risk.md. Hypothesis 3 of the plan cannot be confirmed on this dataset without using the leak. Experiment notebook: notebooks/02_risk_model_experiment.ipynb (variables, fraud rate per variable, mutual information, model versus baseline versus the leak, permutation importance, and a synthetic-label sanity check that the pipeline learns when a signal exists). Cross-table search: notebooks/03_fraud_signal_search.ipynb (customers, products, complaints, interactions, transcripts categorized by the real Jev (all consulta_general, flat distress), digital events, campaign sends, surveys): 140 bins, none lifts the fraud rate by 1.5x with 1,000 rows of support. Country, segment, tenure and transaction type were added to the model on request: held-out ROC AUC 0.497.
options: (a) Report the negative result
(b) Proxy target (say which)
(c) Rules baseline as the signal
questions.recommendation: (a), and probe (b) on the development days; never (leak)

questions.question: With the real Jev, a message that mixes a stolen card with an unrecognized charge came back as tarjeta_robada with confidence 0.55 (probabilities: tarjeta_robada 0.55, cargo_no_reconocido 0.43), so POL-CLARIFY asked a clarification question instead of opening the case and offering the lock. The plan's proposal 'Lectura de las señales de Jev' reads the summed mass of the dispute intents (0.98 here) and clarifies only between 0.30 and 0.70. Adopt the dispute-mass reading (a spec change to POL-CLARIFY), or keep the brief's per-option confidence?
questions.context: Verified 27-Sep on the fixture with jev-1.13.0. The per-option rule costs a turn whenever the customer states two dispute reasons at once, which is common (stolen card plus unrecognized charge). Changing it touches docs/specs/dispute-policy-v2.3.md criterion 8 and the router.
options: Adopt the dispute-mass reading (recommended)
Keep the per-option confidence
questions.recommendation: Adopt the dispute-mass reading
questions.answer: Keep the per-option confidence; do not adopt the dispute-mass reading. The intents stay independent, always: when a message carries several intents (for example stolen card plus unrecognized charge), the clarification lists each detected intent to the customer and asks them to clarify each one separately. The policy never merges intents into a single mass.

questions.topic: Data: fraud claims, fraud flags and call transcripts are independent
questions.question: Over 2023 to 2026 there are 12,297 unrecognized-charge complaints against 4,316 is_fraud flags, and the two never meet: a flagged charge is followed by a claim no more often than an unflagged one (0.35 vs 0.45 percent in 60 days, Fisher p 0.40), claims carry a prior flag at the same rate as branch or service complaints (0.12 percent, chi-square p 0.86), the 3 claims that name the product of a flagged charge match neither amount nor currency, and the 171,321 call transcripts are 42 customer templates with zero fraud, theft or unrecognized words and the same topic mix near flagged and unflagged charges. Can the mentors confirm that the label, the complaints and the transcripts are synthetic and mutually independent, or point us to the linkage we missed (for example an id that ties a complaint to a transaction)?
questions.context: docs/technical-discuss-points.md section 6 and notebooks/04_claims_vs_flags_and_transcript_nlp.ipynb (charts 16 and 17). Closes the search for a learnable fraud signal together with TQ-023: the leak-free model sits at ROC AUC 0.50 because nothing in the data moves with is_fraud. The report presents the independence as a data-quality finding next to the fraud_score leak; no metric of the dispute stack depends on the label.
options: Confirm the independence; the report states it as a data-quality finding (recommended)
There is a linkage we missed; the mentors point to it and notebook 04 reruns
questions.recommendation: Confirm the independence; the report states it as a data-quality finding

questions.topic: ML: fraud risk score transferred from the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection competition
questions.question: is_fraud is random and fraud_score derives from it (TQ-023, TQ-025), so POL-ESC-ML-RISK has no trainable target in the bank data. The proposal (docs/specs/fraud-risk-model-v1-ieee-cis.md) trains the risk model on the public IEEE-CIS competition data (590,540 labeled card-not-present transactions, 3.5 percent fraud) using only a feature contract we can compute on our charges (amount in USD, processing-clock time, credit or debit, card age, days since the previous charge, counts per card and customer in 1, 7 and 30 days, per-card amount mean, std and z-score, address distance bucket, consistency checks, email domain frequency), validates it on the competition's time split with an adversarial check of the domain gap, and serves it through the unchanged RiskScorer with a percentile threshold computed on our serving window (top 2 percent of disputable charges) instead of the absolute 0.70. The identity table has no counterpart: digital_events cannot be tied to a charge (170 of 205,943 Web and App charges of 2026 have an event within an hour, none on the same product). Do the mentors accept the transfer as the model of record, the competition data licence (competition and non-commercial use) for the submission, and the percentile threshold?
questions.context: Replaces the training recipe of brief decision 3, keeps its feature discipline and the leakage guards (no is_fraud, no fraud_score, no post-authorization column). Card-not-present limitation: on POS, ATM and Branch charges the model extrapolates and the rules baseline stays as the second opinion. Until the answer the policy keeps ml_risk_score = 0.0 by default. Notebook 05 (29-Sep) results: the contract is computable on both sources; five features keep as they are, four as per-source ranks, eleven go to the ablation, two are dropped. Raw values separate the sources with adversarial AUC 1.000; on per-source percentile ranks it is 1.000 as well: the gap cannot be transformed away, so only the percentile threshold makes the score usable here. Jev homologated the categorical levels (61 typed answers): credit and debit map at 0.99, the card network and the product codes have no equivalent; the serving rule is Web and App charges only (30 percent of charges, Jev coverage 0.69 and 0.60), rules baseline elsewhere. Levels for the mentors to decide: ProductCD W (0.63 no equivalent versus 0.31 Purchase), DeviceType mobile, Windows, Linux. Trained on 29-Sep with the 19 deployable features (card age excluded: opening dates are independent of the charges): holdout ROC AUC 0.817, PR AUC 0.165; threshold 0.0669 = percentile 98 of 75,366 Web and App charges; agreement with is_fraud 0.507. Wired behind POL-ESC-ML-RISK with the threshold read from the input.
options: Accept the IEEE-CIS transfer with the percentile threshold (recommended)
Accept the transfer but keep the absolute 0.70 threshold from the brief
Reject external data; report the negative result of TQ-023 and leave POL-ESC-ML-RISK without a model
questions.recommendation: Accept the IEEE-CIS transfer with the percentile threshold
questions.answer: Accept the IEEE-CIS transfer. POL-ESC-ML-RISK escalates to HITL by the percentile threshold computed on the serving window; the fixed 0.70 threshold is not used. The model of record uses only the homologated (deployable) variables. Follow-up process: cherry-pick, among the roughly 400 competition variables left out, the ones the agent can consume so the fraud score improves after the interview with the customer (candidates in reports/ml/ieee_cis_feature_importance.md). The mentors' answer on the competition data licence stays pending.

The keyword lists are broad substrings, which is why the statement precedence now needs a charge word next to the dispute keyword ("¿Cuál es mi saldo? Ya pregunté dos veces" keeps abstaining). On the Jev path Jev's own intent decides and this rule does not apply.
options: Keep it: only the statement yields to dispute language (recommended)
Extend it to insurance and card-support charges
Extend it to every out-of-scope category

questions.topic: Orchestrator: bank outages (reason code, retries, a missed lock offer)
questions.question: When a bank read fails or times out, the turn now goes to a human with the new escalation reason SYSTEM_OF_RECORD_UNAVAILABLE and confirms nothing (brief section 5, pr/8). Three decisions: (1) keep the new code, which the labeling README now lists, or fold it into ACTION_VERIFICATION_FAILED; (2) add bounded retries before the handoff, as brief section 3.3 proposes (2 retries), and a Postgres statement timeout (today only a 5-second connect timeout); (3) when the card list fails while offering the lock to a customer who reported a stolen card, the offer is dropped and audited as LOCK_NOT_OFFERED and the verified case number still reaches the customer: should a human also get a handoff to offer the lock?
questions.context: ops_handoffs.escalation_reason has no CHECK, so the new code needs no migration; the console shows the reason as text. A lock that times out after the customer's yes already takes the pending-lock path with ACTION_VERIFICATION_FAILED, because the write may or may not have happened. Failures of the ops store itself are not handled yet.
options: Keep the new code, add 2 bounded retries in the gateways and hand off the missed lock offer (recommended)
Keep the new code and today's behavior
Fold the outage into ACTION_VERIFICATION_FAILED
questions.recommendation: Keep the new code, add 2 bounded retries in the gateways and hand off the missed lock offer
questions.answer: Keep the new code, add 2 bounded retries in the gateways and hand off the missed lock offer. To implement, with tests.

Keep the generic texts
End the conversation after the lock answer

questions.answer: Add a question for loss-only reports and reword the refused reply. A policy text change: it needs the spec update with the code.

questions.topic: ML: a missing USD value scores as 0.0 at serving time, as in training
questions.question: rows_to_canonical read the local amount as USD when amount_usd was None, so a 480,000 COP charge would enter the features as 480,000 USD, while training (load_bank_canonical) reads amount_usd as stored and the feature builder fills a missing value with 0.0. Since d81ef41 (pr/8) serving passes the stored value through, so a missing value scores as 0.0, as in training. Confirm?
questions.context: Until pr/8 the DuckDB gateway returned NaN for a NULL amount_usd, and NaN scored as 0.0; once the gateway returns None, as Postgres does, the old fallback would have read the local amount as USD. On Postgres bank.transactions.amount_usd is NOT NULL (0003_bank.sql), so the fallback never ran there. Gold holds no NULL amount_usd after the silver fix (spec S9), so only data defects reach this path, and POL-DISP-TYPE escalates such a charge with DATA_GAP_AMOUNT_USD whatever the score.
options: Confirm: score a missing USD value as 0.0 (recommended)
Restore the local-amount fallback
questions.recommendation: Confirm: score a missing USD value as 0.0
questions.answer: Confirm: score a missing USD value as 0.0, as in training.

The blind table lives only in the PR #12 description and in a git-ignored handoff note; TQ-019 decides where reports live in the repo.
options: Present the blind run as the held-out result and the 0f663d7 run as post-error-analysis, each with its commit (recommended)
Build a held-out v2 before the final report and present its first run as the held-out result
questions.recommendation: Present the blind run as the held-out result and the 0f663d7 run as post-error-analysis, each with its commit
questions.answer: Present the blind run as the held-out result and the 0f663d7 run as post-error-analysis, each with its commit.

questions.topic: Eval: the denominator of the safe automated resolution rate
questions.question: The official statement defines safe automated resolution as a "rate over all in-scope cases, plus the share where automation was attempted" (AGENTS.md section 5), while the brief and src/eval/metrics.py divide by eligible cases only (expected outcome AUTONOMOUS_RESOLUTION). Which denominator do we report, and what counts as in-scope?
questions.context: Audit v3, AUD-10. The adversarial review of 26-Sep (item 3) flagged the gap and no decision followed. reports/eval_dev.md already prints the eligible rate (9 of 9) and the attempted-automation share (9 of 18). In-scope could mean every dispute conversation (without out-of-scope intents such as DEV-006, a loan request, and without the token or cross-customer attacks), or every case of the suite.
options: Report both: over eligible cases, and over in-scope cases defined as dispute conversations without out-of-scope intents or API attacks (recommended)
Report only the rate over all in-scope cases, as the official wording says
Keep the eligible-cases denominator only
questions.recommendation: Report both: over eligible cases, and over in-scope cases defined as dispute conversations without out-of-scope intents or API attacks
questions.answer: Report both: over eligible cases, and over in-scope cases defined as dispute conversations without out-of-scope intents or API attacks. To implement in src/eval/metrics.py.

questions.topic: Eval: an abstention on a case that needed a human
questions.question: The judge (src/eval/runner.py) flags materially_incorrect_outcome only when the system resolves alone a case that needed an abstention or a human. When it abstains or clarifies on a case that needed a human, as in HO-139 and HO-143 (disputes above 500 USD answered as out of scope), the case counts only as a missed transfer. Should it also count as an unsafe outcome?
questions.context: Audit v3, AUD-31. AGENTS.md section 5 counts materially wrong results as unsafe outcomes; telling a customer that a dispute above 500 USD is out of scope leaves them with no case and no human. Changing the judge changes the reported numbers, so record the decision before the next runs are reported.
options: Count it as unsafe (materially_incorrect_outcome) and keep it among the missed transfers (recommended)
Keep it as a missed transfer only
questions.recommendation: Count it as unsafe (materially_incorrect_outcome) and keep it among the missed transfers
questions.answer: Count it as unsafe (materially_incorrect_outcome) and keep it among the missed transfers. To implement in the judge (src/eval/runner.py); the suite's cases do not change.

questions.question: OpenTelemetry stayed in scope on 26-Sep ("sin recortes") and was scheduled for day 6, and nothing of it exists in src/. Do we drop it formally, or add a minimal version?
questions.context: Audit v3, AUD-08. The append-only audit log already records every action with its conversation and actor. An OpenTelemetry middleware makes Vercel keep the static files inside the function unless cdn = true is forced (docs/SUPABASE_VERCEL.md section 6), and adds dependencies to a bundle that may already exceed 500 MB (AUD-30).
options: Drop it formally in the decision log and declare it future work (recommended)
Minimal: a request trace_id in the audit log and the response headers, no exporter
Full OpenTelemetry with an exporter
questions.recommendation: Drop it formally in the decision log and declare it future work
questions.answer: Drop it formally in the decision log and declare it future work. The append-only audit log (ops.audit_log) already records every turn, action and actor with full auditability; full OpenTelemetry would inflate the Vercel function bundle and risk cold-start timeouts without adding value for the hackathon submission.

questions.topic: RAG: which policy clauses and parameters the policy explainer may tell a customer
questions.question: The RAG roadmap indexes the 13 clause ids of spec v2.3 and answers customers with the clause it retrieves. Should each clause carry an exposure level: internal for POL-AUT-150, POL-SEC-SESSION and POL-ESC-ML-RISK (indexed, but answered with a fixed redirect that states none of their content), public_generic for POL-ESC-LEGAL and POL-ESC-DISTRESS (a specialist reviews some cases, without naming what triggers it), and public for the rest, stating only the parameters the policy texts already tell customers (60 days, 500 USD, 48 hours)?
questions.context: The spec says the customer never hears that credit was applied (POL-AUT-150 row) and rule 8 keeps provisional credit inside the handoff packet, so a question such as "¿me devuelven la plata?" must not surface the credit criteria. POL-SEC-SESSION is an auth control outside the dispute policy, and POL-ESC-ML-RISK is the fraud model's escalation threshold. Listing the legal and distress triggers would tell customers which words reach a human. dispute_policy.py already tells customers 60 days (line 387), 500 USD (line 200) and 48 hours (line 212); no customer text states 150 USD or the risk threshold. Indexing the internal clauses lets a credit question land on a safe redirect instead of the nearest public clause. Task 1.1 of docs/RAG_IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md waits on this answer.
options: Exposure levels as proposed, internal clauses indexed and answered with a fixed redirect (recommended)
Same exposure levels, but leave the internal clauses out of the corpus
questions.recommendation: Exposure levels as proposed, internal clauses indexed and answered with a fixed redirect
questions.answer: Exposure levels as proposed, internal clauses indexed and answered with a fixed redirect. Applied in data/policy_corpus.json (roadmap Task 1.1); the formal reply in 3 to 5 business days, which the intake text already states, joins the public parameters under the same rule.

questions.topic: ML and policy: what a disputed charge in a risk zone should trigger
questions.question: Since 3-Oct a deterministic risk zone validator (src/tools/risk_zone.py) runs beside the learned risk score on every identified charge: it names where the charge was made against the customer's country and city on file (HOME, DOMESTIC_OTHER_CITY, ABROAD, UNKNOWN), and ABROAD is the risk zone. Today its verdict is a fact for the human agent only (the handoff packet and the audit row RISK_ZONE_VALIDATED); it changes no outcome and never reaches the customer. Should a charge in a risk zone trigger something more: (a) nothing, the verdict stays advisory; (b) a mandatory escalation to a human under a new clause, also on the channels the model does not score; (c) the preventive card lock offer with the customer's confirmation, which needs a new reason code in the ops.card_locks CHECK and a migration?
questions.context: Kmilo asked on 3-Oct for a parallel validator of whether the transaction is in a risk zone, after proposing a hold with a message to the customer for charges made in a high-risk zone. Measured on the 251,398 charges of the 60 days to 2026-06-17 (data/lakehouse_full.duckdb, derived from the organizer's data): 95.1 percent HOME, 0.3 percent DOMESTIC_OTHER_CITY, 4.6 percent ABROAD, the same on every channel. On the 75,366 Web and App charges the model scores, 1,508 are above its threshold (2.0 percent) and 3,441 are abroad: both checks flag 180, only the model 1,328, only the zone 3,261; an abroad charge is above the threshold 5.23 percent of the time against 1.85 percent for the rest. On the 176,032 charges of the channels the model does not score (70.0 percent), 8,120 are abroad and no risk check read them before. Abroad charges at or under 500 USD, which option (b) would move from intake to a human, are 2.46 percent of the window. Limits: the data has a country and a city per charge and nothing finer (28 cities, coordinates 81 percent null), so no map of zones inside a city can be joined; is_fraud carries no learnable signal (TQ-023), so no place can be ranked by fraud rate from this data, and an external zone map needs a cited source with its provenance label (rule 4). A hold at authorization time is a second workflow (rule 1): the dispute flow acts after the charge. Options (b) and (c) change policy v2.3 (spec, traceability matrix, policy corpus) and the outcomes of the frozen held-out suite, whose design labels follow v2.3. docs/technical-discuss-points.md section 9.
options: Advisory only: a verified fact for the human agent (recommended until the team decides)
A new mandatory escalation clause for a charge in a risk zone
The preventive card lock offer for a charge in a risk zone, with the customer's confirmation
questions.recommendation: Advisory only: a verified fact for the human agent

questions.topic: Dispute flow: sibling charges on the same card, merchant and process day
questions.question: When a customer disputes one charge and the same card shows more disputable charges at the same merchant on the same process day, should those sibling charges only be told (to the customer once the case is open, to the specialist in the handoff), or should a burst of them also escalate the turn with the lock offer, as POL-ESC-MULTI does for three disputed charges?
questions.context: Branch feat/sibling-charges, 3-Oct. Today they are told and never counted: spec v2.3 defines POL-ESC-MULTI over disputed charges, and a charge the customer has not disowned is not one (spec assumption S20). The scenario behind the question is a compromised point of sale that repeats charges on one card in one night. The supplied data cannot measure it: the bank rows carry no terminal id, 77.9 % of the sample rows have no merchant on record, and no card holds more than two transactions on one process day (docs/technical-discuss-points.md section 10), so the behavior is shown on team-generated fixtures only. Counting undisputed charges would send customers with several legitimate purchases at one merchant to a human, which lowers safe automated resolution.
options: Tell only: the customer and the specialist see them, POL-ESC-MULTI keeps counting disputed charges (recommended, in code)
Also escalate a burst: the disputed charge plus two or more siblings goes to a human with the MULTI_CHARGE_FRAUD lock offer (a spec change: new clause input and tests)
Keep only the handoff fact and remove the note from the customer reply
questions.recommendation: Tell only: the customer and the specialist see them, POL-ESC-MULTI keeps counting disputed charges

questions.topic: Data and conversation: how a charge without a merchant reaches the agent and the customer
questions.question: Since 4-Oct gold_transactions.merchant_name tells two cases apart: 'Not Applicable' on a Withdrawal, Transfer, Payment, Deposit or Adjustment (the dataset never gives those types a merchant) and 'Unknown Merchant' on a purchase that lost its merchant. The label is text inside a name column, so each reader compares strings to know it is not a name, and it reaches the agent only on the local DuckDB path: the deployed API reads the Postgres copy and the frozen held-out suite keeps 'Unknown Merchant'. Two things to decide. (1) Should both gateways return a typed field beside the name (merchant_status: named, missing, not_applicable), computed by one rule, so the orchestrator and the handoff stop reading labels? (2) What should the customer see in the list of recent charges for a charge without a merchant: the label as today (English), or a description built from what the data has (the type in the customer's language, the payment category, the city)?
questions.context: Kmilo asked on 4-Oct why so many charges read 'Unknown Merchant' and for gold to say 'Not Applicable' on internal transactions. Measured on data/lakehouse_full.duckdb (derived from the organizer's data): merchant_name is NULL on 76.7 percent of the 4,425,008 transactions; all 3,341,602 Withdrawal, Transfer, Payment, Deposit and Adjustment rows have no merchant, on every channel, and 54,172 of 1,083,406 purchases (5.0 percent) lost theirs. Purchases are 29.3 percent of the disputable charges of the 60-day window, so a merchant can help on fewer than a third of them. What the data has instead: transaction_category on 95 percent of the payments (not in gold today); transaction_city on 90 percent and transaction_country on every row (both in gold). branch_id, on 95 percent of the ATM and Branch channel charges, is not the place of the charge: it is always a branch of the customer's country, and its city equals the charge's own city on 17.5 percent of the rows that have one, so it is left out. No policy outcome depends on the label. Option (2) changes text the customer reads, and a typed field in the gateway rows needs the same column in the eval bank fixture. docs/technical-discuss-points.md section 11.
options: Typed merchant_status in both gateways, and a description of the charge in the customer's language for the list (recommended)
Typed merchant_status in both gateways only; the customer keeps seeing the label
Keep the labels in gold as they are and compare strings
questions.recommendation: Typed merchant_status in both gateways, and a description of the charge in the customer's language for the list

questions.topic: Conversation: several rules questions after a greeting end with a human
questions.question: After a greeting, the first rules question reaches the policy explainer, but the next one takes the dispute flow and a third one is escalated to a human with POL-ESC-AMBIG, although the customer disputed nothing. Should a message that the explainer answered stop counting as an earlier dispute?
questions.context: Read from the code on 4-Oct and reproduced on 5-Oct by tests/test_policy_rag.py::test_rules_questions_after_a_greeting_keep_reaching_the_explainer_and_never_a_human (an expected failure until this is decided). The question '¿Cuántos días tengo para disputar un cargo?' carries intent cargo_no_reconocido because it names 'un cargo', and _disputed_earlier in src/orchestrator/dispute_orchestrator.py reads any earlier intent other than consulta_general as a dispute. In the reproduction the second question gets 'No encontramos un cargo que coincida con su descripción' and the third opens a handoff. The explainer is on in production (data/rag_gate.json). No held-out case asks a rules question, so the suite does not see it (reports/eval_heldout_explainer.md). A fix needs its own test and, per the rule for cases found by hand, the approval of Daniel and Kmilo.
options: An earlier message with policy_question set never counts as a dispute, and a rules question never adds a clarification attempt (recommended)
Keep the behavior and state it as a limit
Turn the explainer off until it is fixed (remove data/rag_gate.json)
questions.recommendation: An earlier message with policy_question set never counts as a dispute, and a rules question never adds a clarification attempt

questions.topic: Conversation: the language is fixed by the first message
questions.question: The conversation language is set while the state is new and never changes afterwards. A customer who greets in Spanish and then writes the dispute in Portuguese gets the case confirmation in Spanish. Should each reply follow the language of the message it answers?
questions.context: Read from the code on 4-Oct (handle_message in src/orchestrator/dispute_orchestrator.py takes understanding.language only in state new) and reproduced on 5-Oct by tests/test_policy_rag.py::test_a_customer_who_switches_to_portuguese_after_the_first_message_is_answered_in_portuguese (an expected failure until this is decided). The dispute itself is understood: the case opens. No held-out conversation changes language, and the 2 reply-language misses of the suite (HO-245, HO-250) are single messages that mix both. A one-word reply such as 'sim' or 'no' carries little language signal, so following the last message needs a rule for short replies.
options: Follow the language of each message, keeping the conversation language for option, yes and no replies (recommended)
Keep the first-message language and state it as a limit
Follow the language picker of the chat instead of detecting it
questions.recommendation: Follow the language of each message, keeping the conversation language for option, yes and no replies

questions.topic: ML: floating-point residue in two features of the risk contract
questions.question: amount_zscore_card and tx_sum_card_7d of the feature contract (v1.1) carry floating-point residue. When a card's earlier amounts are all equal, the variance is a tiny positive number instead of zero and the z-score divides by it. Should a spread under a small epsilon count as zero (contract 1.2, model retrained), or does the model of record keep v1.1?
questions.context: Found on 5-Oct by the EDA of the 19 served features (reports/ml/risk_feature_eda.md). On the IEEE-CIS competition amount_zscore_card runs from about -67 million to 528 million; 308 of 590,540 rows pass 1,000 in absolute value, 667 pass 50, and 2,355 have a card spread between 0 and 0.001. On the bank's Web and App window the maximum is 609.83. tx_sum_card_7d has a median of 3.0e-09 instead of 0 for the same reason (a running sum minus the current amount). The model reads per-source percentile ranks, so the effect is bounded to those rows, but their rank is noise: the sign of the residue decides whether the row ranks at the bottom or at the top. Fixing it changes the features, so the bundle, its threshold and reports/eval_heldout_model.md would be regenerated. The retrain is reproducible since 5-Oct (rows load in a fixed order).
options: Fix it after the submission as contract 1.2, retrain and re-measure (recommended)
Fix it now and regenerate the reports before the submission
Keep contract 1.1 and state the residue as a limit
questions.recommendation: Fix it after the submission as contract 1.2, retrain and re-measure
questions.source: 5-Oct, EDA of the risk features; src/ml/feature_contract.py
